Title: Implement the Actions/Tasks domain in packages/models
Description:
Context: design/actions/models.md and design/actions/wireframes.md fully specify an Action/Task domain, but there is currently no packages/models/src/actions directory at all - this is pure design, 0% implemented. Nearly everything else this session touched (Observe's Task-completion tie-in, the Workbook page, Calendar's Actions pane) depends on this existing first.

Build: schema.ts (Action and Task Triplit collections - Action has targetType/plant/plantingArea/workspace/garden/name/description/tasks, with NO stored completed or assignees, since both are derived from its Tasks; Task has type/date/dateOverridden/name/description/assignees/completed), commands.ts (Zod create/update schemas), controller.ts, index.ts, following the same Domain Model Pattern as packages/models/src/plants. Implement: the TaskType enum (Seed/Germinate/Flower/Thin/Harden/Transplant/Harvest/Expire/Prune/Cover a planting area/Weed a planting area/Till a planting area/Tidy a workspace/Apply fertilizer/Irrigate/Other), the dateOverridden flag (date is normally recomputed from the Plant's expectedLifespan/Cultivar timing and stops being recomputed once a user manually reschedules), and the two-path completion rule for the six types with a matching Observe type (Seed/Germinate/Flower/Transplant/Harvest/Expire): completing directly writes a minimal PlantObservation with today's date, or completing happens automatically when a full observation of the matching type is recorded through Observe. Also wire Action auto-generation/maintenance off Plant creation and edits as described in the models doc.

Read design/actions/models.md in full before starting - it is the canonical spec.

Out of scope: the Workbook UI itself (separate task), Observe's UI (separate task, already partly built for Plants).

Title: Build the Workbook page
Description:
Context: apps/web's workbook +page.svelte (apps/web/src/routes/gardens/[gardenId]/(planner)/workbook/+page.svelte) is a literal UnderConstructionPage placeholder. design/actions/wireframes.md fully specifies what it should be.

Build: the Workbook per design/actions/wireframes.md - a My Tasks/All Tasks scope toggle (default My Tasks), a dated agenda grouped by date then assignee, an always-visible Unassigned bucket, bidirectional assignment (assign another User, or self-claim from Unassigned), tap-to-complete per Task (with inline expansion to fill in type-specific fields like Harvest mass before confirming - the actual completion rule itself lives in Actions models, don't re-derive it here), and real-time collaboration (a Task completed by one User should disappear from everyone else's agenda immediately via Triplit's live queries).

Depends on the Actions/Tasks domain task being done first (no schema exists yet to build this against).

Read design/actions/wireframes.md in full before starting.

Title: Implement DraftBucket and wire it into Add Plants' commit/discard flow
Description:
Context: design/planner/wireframes.md's Add Plants section and design/plants/models.md's DraftBucket section specify that staged plants in the 'To Create' bucket are ordinary Plant rows referencing a DraftBucket, not a separate draft-shaped entity - this was a deliberate architecture decision made after considering and rejecting a separate PlantDraft entity (see design/plants/models.md for the reasoning, it's worth reading to understand why before changing anything). None of this exists in code: no draftBuckets collection, no draftBucketId on Plant. packages/ui/src/components/verdagraph/tools/PlantsCreateForm.svelte currently submits directly via the plantsCreate command with no draft/commit step at all.

Build: a draftBuckets Triplit collection (name, creator, and Plants reference it via a nullable draftBucketId rather than the bucket holding a list), following the same pattern as PlantGroup. Add draftBucketId to the Plant schema. Update Action-generation to skip Plants with a non-null draftBucketId (Actions/Tasks are only created once a Plant is no longer part of any open DraftBucket). Update any 'official garden state' reads (yield totals, future generator inputs) to filter draftBucketId == null - centralize this as a shared query helper rather than scattering the filter. Wire PlantsCreateForm/the 'To Create' tree to stage into a DraftBucket instead of submitting directly; committing a DraftBucket is just deleting the bucket (the Plants already exist and don't change); discarding is deleting the Plants in it.

Read design/plants/models.md's DraftBucket section and design/planner/wireframes.md's Add Plants section (especially 'Drafts are persisted, not local state') before starting.

Out of scope: ghost rendering in Layout/Calendar (separate tasks, though they depend on this), Patterns and Generators (separate tasks, both depend on this existing).

Title: Implement GrowthStage and IconPack, wire Color/ExpectedGeometry into Layout icon rendering
Description:
Context: Cultivar's ColorProfile and ExpectedGeometryProfile already exist in packages/models/src/cultivars/attributes but are not referenced anywhere in the Layout/canvas rendering code (verified - zero hits for baseColor/outlineColor/ExpectedGeometryProfile in packages/ui/src/components/canvas or verdagraph). GrowthStage and IconPack don't exist in code at all yet; both are specified in design/plants/models.md (#growthstage) and design/cultivars/models.md (#iconpack-provisional).

Build: (1) GrowthStage as a derived/computed function in packages/models (not a stored field) - given a Plant's active Lifespan, compute one of seed/vegetative/producing/dormant/expired from its observations, per the exact boundary rules in design/plants/models.md (note 'producing' deliberately merges what used to be separate flowering/harvesting stages - read the reasoning, don't re-split it). Handle the origin degradation case (seedToTransplant/seedlingToTransplant Plants may have no plant-seed/plant-germ observation) and the perennial repeat-cycle case (multiple plant-flower/plant-dormancy-enter/plant-growth-enter observations over the Plant's life, no special cardinality handling needed since observations is already a many-relation). (2) An iconPacks/iconPackVariants schema (name, owner, visibility mirroring CultivarCollection's HIDDEN/UNLISTED/PUBLIC, one IconPackVariant per GrowthStage it covers) and a Cultivar.iconPackId field. (3) Wire the Layout's Plant icon rendering to actually use Cultivar.baseColor/outlineColor/textColor and the abbreviation for the default icon, falling back from IconPack SVGs when no pack is set, sized/shaped by whichever Geometry entry is active for the focused day (recorded if present else expected).

Read design/plants/models.md's GrowthStage section and design/planner/wireframes.md's Layout section ('Default icon', 'Icon packs') before starting.

Out of scope: aggregate-plant rendering, ghosting, selection/popups, interplanting lines (all separate tasks below).

Title: Add InterplantingProfile and render it as dotted lines in Layout
Description:
Context: design/cultivars/models.md specifies a new (not yet implemented) Cultivar attribute profile for interplanting distance, and design/planner/wireframes.md's Layout section specifies how it renders.

Build: an InterplantingProfile attribute (a single minimumDistance field in meters - deliberately a scalar, not a per-Cultivar-pair table, see the doc for why) added to the Cultivar attributes composition the same way Color/ExpectedGeometry are structured. In the Layout, render a dotted line around a Plant's icon at that radius when the Plant is selected or hovered (not for every Plant at once - that would clutter the grid).

Depends on the GrowthStage/IconPack task's Layout rendering work being in place first, since this hooks into the same icon rendering pass.

Read design/cultivars/models.md's Interplanting section and design/planner/wireframes.md's Layout section ('Interplanting') before starting.

Title: Build the Observe toolbox tool
Description:
Context: packages/ui/src/components/verdagraph/tools/ObserveForm.svelte is currently a 1-line stub. design/planner/wireframes.md fully specifies it - it's one of the more involved tools since it introduces the batch-with-per-plant-override pattern.

Build: a type selector (Seed/Germinate/Flower/Enter Dormancy/Exit Dormancy/Transplant/Harvest/Expire) that swaps in that type's fields (mostly a date, defaulting to the Timeline Selector's focused day; mass/quality/description for Harvest - quality should offer defective/passable/average/exceptional as data-entry suggestions, not an enforced enum, since the underlying field is free text; a destination Location/Geometry for Transplant). A 'To Record' tree driven by the existing shared plant selection, not a separate picker. Every entry in that tree must be independently expandable to override its own date and type-specific fields - this applies to every type, not just Harvest. No draft/commit step - submitting writes straight onto the selected Plants' recorded data (this is real, already-happened data, unlike Add Plants). Recording a type with a matching Task type also completes that Plant's open Task of the same type (see the Actions domain task for the underlying rule).

Read design/planner/wireframes.md's Observe section in full before starting.

Depends on the Actions/Tasks domain task for the Task-completion tie-in to mean anything yet.

Title: Build the Translate and Delete toolbox tools
Description:
Context: both packages/ui/src/components/verdagraph/tools/TranslateForm.svelte and DeleteForm.svelte are 1-line stubs. Both are small, well-scoped tools - bundling them since neither needs its own long session.

Build Translate: edits ONLY a Plant's expectedLifespan Location/Geometry (never recorded data - that's Observe's Transplant type's job, see design/planner/wireframes.md for why this split exists). Two modes: an exact destination coordinate for one Plant, and a numeric (Δx, Δy) offset applied to the whole current selection at once - this offset case is the main reason Translate exists as a tool rather than relying on Layout's free-hand drag alone.

Build Delete: operates on the shared plant selection, no picker of its own. Destructive with no undo, so requires an explicit confirmation naming how many Plants are about to be deleted. Deleting a Plant must cascade-delete its Actions/Tasks.

Read design/planner/wireframes.md's Translate and Delete sections before starting.

Title: Build the Patterns toolbox tool
Description:
Context: packages/ui/src/components/verdagraph/tools/PatternsForm.svelte is currently a 1-line stub (literally contains the word 'patterns'). design/planner/wireframes.md and design/cultivars/models.md specify it fully.

Build: a library view of saved Pattern templates (name, owner - User or Garden - following the same HIDDEN/UNLISTED/PUBLIC visibility model as CultivarCollection). An editor that reuses the exact same Form/To Create bucket editor Add Plants uses, but disconnected from the live Layout/Timeline Selector - since a Pattern isn't tied to a real Workspace or date, its spatial canvas and timeline work in offsets relative to one origin in the bucket instead of absolute coordinates/dates. JSON export/import so Patterns can move between Gardens or be shared outside the app.

Depends on the DraftBucket task - a Pattern is essentially an unattached DraftBucket edited in relative-coordinate mode, so build that first.

Read design/planner/wireframes.md's Patterns section and design/cultivars/models.md's IconPack section (same ownership/visibility pattern, worth comparing) before starting.

Title: Build the Generators toolbox tool
Description:
Context: packages/ui/src/components/verdagraph/tools/GeneratorsForm.svelte is a 1-line stub, and there is no Generator schema or algorithm anywhere in packages/models - this is 100% design only (design/planner/models.md). The 'Generators' mention in code today is only the Toolbox registration (label + icon), nothing functional.

Build: a form closely mirroring the Generator/GeneratorObjective models - Horizon (number, days), Strategy (a select; Simulated Annealing is the only option for now but make it a select since the model anticipates more), Objective (a repeatable list of {objective type, weight} rows - PlantPercentages/Calories/NutrientProfile/Biodiversity/PollinatorStrength/MinimalLabour), and Include/Exclude Plants (two Cultivar-name multi-selects). Running a Generator must NOT write to the model directly - it should produce a new DraftBucket, reviewed/edited/committed or discarded exactly like a manually-built one. A full simulated-annealing optimizer is a big lift with no existing research in this repo to build from (planner/models.md says as much) - a first pass can use a much simpler placement heuristic as a placeholder for the real algorithm; flag that explicitly in the PR rather than silently under-delivering on 'simulated annealing'.

Depends on the DraftBucket task.

Read design/planner/wireframes.md's Generators section and design/planner/models.md's Generator section before starting.

Title: Build the Cultivar Collections editor
Description:
Context: apps/web's (config)/cultivars/+page.svelte is a literal UnderConstructionPage placeholder. There's an orphaned previous attempt at apps/web/src/lib/data/cultivar/{commands,queries,schemas}.ts.old - worth reading before starting to see what was already tried and abandoned, rather than starting completely blind. design/cultivars/wireframes.md specifies the intended design.

Build: a collection page pairing a tree (reuse the same EditableTree pattern already built for Tree's PlantTree/PlantingWindowTree - NOT a flat list, since both CultivarCollections and Cultivars have their own independent parent/child inheritance hierarchies that a flat list can't represent) against a detail pane for whichever node is selected. Collection-level metadata (name, slug, visibility, description, tags, parent) editable above the tree. Cultivar detail is one flat form, not a wizard: top-level fields first (names, abbreviation, scientificName, description, parent, iconPackId), then a collapsible section per attribute profile (Annual Lifecycle, Frost Date Planting Windows, Origin, Color, Expected Geometry, Interplanting once it exists, Temperature once Environment observations exist). Every field, top-level or in a profile section, should use the existing Form.Label/FormInfoPopover pattern (see packages/ui/src/components/verdagraph/tools/PlantsCreateFormModeSingle.svelte for an example) to surface its Zod .describe() text on click - reuse this, don't invent a new explanation UI.

Read design/cultivars/wireframes.md in full before starting.

Title: Calendar: Cultivar grouping, filtering, interactive info-point popups, and selection integration
Description:
Context: packages/ui/src/components/rangeCalendar/ is substantially built (a real nested melt-Tree view with expected/recorded child bars and info points), but several things specified in design/planner/wireframes.md's Calendar section aren't there yet: (1) the Plants pane is flat, not grouped by Cultivar (Tree already groups Cultivar>Plant - Calendar should match). (2) There's no PlantGroup-tag filter, and the Actions pane (itself unbuilt - depends on the Actions domain task) needs My/All-scope, assignee, TaskType, completed/incomplete, and Workspace/PlantingArea/Environment filters. (3) Info point popups are minimal - expected-lifespan observations only have move-by-day/week buttons (RangeCalendarPane.svelte), recorded-lifespan observations have NO popup at all (explicitly commented out in items/plants.ts), and neither supports edit/delete/record-for-real/complete-a-task actions. (4) Same-day info points currently just render in a fixed spot with no collision handling - need the shrink-and-pack-with-overflow-badge behavior (2-3 actual icons, then a +N badge beyond that). (5) Calendar's melt-Tree selection doesn't sync with the shared SelectionManager at all (onSelectedChange is commented out in rangeCalendar/context.svelte.ts) - Tree already does this for Plants (see PlantTree.svelte lines ~110-134) as the reference implementation to follow.

Read design/planner/wireframes.md's entire Calendar section (Plants pane, PlantingWindows pane, Actions pane, Info point popups) before starting - it's long but this task touches most of it.

Depends on the Actions/Tasks domain task for the Actions pane, and the Observe tool existing for the popup actions to hand off to.

Title: Layout: selection, popups, multi-workspace toggle and tiling, drag-box semantics
Description:
Context: the Planner canvas (packages/ui/src/components/canvas) currently renders Plants but has none of the interaction model design/planner/wireframes.md's Layout section specifies: no selection-on-click, no popups, no multi-workspace support, no drag-box. This is one of the largest remaining gaps. Per AGENTS.md, a Konva-to-native-SVG migration is planned but not started - build this against the current Konva setup, don't block on the migration.

Build: (1) Clicking a Plant adds it to the shared plant SelectionManager and opens a popup - single-Plant selected gets instant single-tap actions (record an observation defaulting to the GrowthStage-implied next type, complete an open Task, delete via a hand-off to the Delete tool to preserve its confirmation step); multi-Plant selected gets a condensed summary and every action becomes a hand-off to Observe/Workbook/Delete pre-scoped to the selection instead of an inline tap. (2) A drag-box selection using intersection (touching, not full-enclosure) combined with the standard editor convention - plain drag replaces, Shift adds, Alt subtracts, Shift+Alt intersects. (3) A Workspaces toggle in the Toolbar (extend the existing single-select Workspace Editor 'Workspaces' menu pattern to support toggling more than one on, defaulting to just one), each enabled Workspace getting its own resizable pane (reuse the existing Resizable.Pane mechanism, not a new docking system), with Calendar's and Layout's own Plant/PlantingWindow queries broadening to every enabled Workspace. Cross-pane dragging (for drag-to-transplant between two Workspace panes) is explicitly OUT of scope here - it's parked pending the SVG migration, see design doc.

Read design/planner/wireframes.md's Layout section in full (Selection, Multiple workspaces) before starting.

Depends on: the GrowthStage/IconPack task (icon rendering this popup sits on top of), the DraftBucket task (ghost styling), the Observe/Delete tool tasks (what the popup hands off to).

Title: Fix the Timeline Selector drag-translate bug
Description:
Context: design/planner/wireframes.md's Timeline Selector section documents a real, precisely-diagnosed bug in packages/ui/src/components/timeline/timelineSelection.svelte.ts's updateSlider function. Dragging the focus thumb is supposed to translate the whole range (begin/focus/end) together, preserving both the range length and the focus-to-edge distances. Instead, updateSlider clamps the new begin and end values INDEPENDENTLY against the slider's own min/max bounds rather than clamping the translation delta itself - so once the end of the range hits the edge of the slider, it gets pinned there while focus keeps moving, and the range visibly shrinks instead of the whole thing just stopping at the boundary.

Fix: compute deltaDays from the focus thumb's movement, reduce that delta (once) if applying it to either begin or end would exceed minSliderValue/maxSliderValue, then apply that same clamped delta uniformly to beginSelection, focus, and endSelection together - not independently clamp each endpoint after the fact.

This is a small, well-isolated fix - read design/planner/wireframes.md's Timeline Selector section for the full writeup, then go straight to updateSlider in timelineSelection.svelte.ts.

Title: Workspace Editor: fill in Environment/Translate/Delete/Expire stubs, add a Move Workspace tool, and implement Environment observations
Description:
Context: several Workspace Editor toolbox tools are thinner than assumed - EnvironmentCreateForm.svelte, TranslateForm.svelte, and DeleteForm.svelte are all 1-line stubs, and ExpireForm.svelte is a completely empty file (0 lines). Only PlantingAreaCreateForm.svelte (346 lines) and LayoutConfigForm.svelte (55 lines, just a 'Controls Position' select plus a commented-out grid-spacing field) have real content. There is also no 'Move Workspace' tool anywhere (distinct from Translate, which moves a PlantingArea/Environment within a Workspace, not the Workspace itself), and no Environment observation types exist anywhere in packages/models - packages/models/src/observations/ids.ts only contains PlantObservationIds today.

Build: (1) EnvironmentCreateForm, TranslateForm, DeleteForm, ExpireForm for the Workspace Editor, following the same patterns as PlantingAreaCreateForm/LayoutConfigForm. (2) A new tool for repositioning a Workspace's own spatial reference (not something inside it) - this is also what the Planner's multi-workspace tiling will eventually need, to arrange which Workspace sits where relative to others. (3) A new set of Environment observation types (e.g. a measured temperature reading, a frost event) added to the generic Observation system the same way Plant's observations.ts defines PlantSeedObservation etc., plus a recording UI - reachable from the Workspace Editor AND as a quick-action on an Environment's group header in the Planner's Calendar PlantingWindows pane / Tree (see design/planner/wireframes.md's 'Environment observations' section). This is also what finally makes Cultivar's TemperatureProfile (deliberately kept unimplemented until now, see design/cultivars/models.md) worth implementing - comparing a Cultivar's expected temperature range against what's actually been recorded.

Read design/workspaces/wireframes.md and design/planner/wireframes.md's 'Environment observations' section before starting.

Title: Migrate the Planner canvas from Konva to native SVG
Description:
Context: AGENTS.md already documents this as a deliberate, specified future step - it is NOT flagged as something to start opportunistically right now, so treat this task's priority as reflecting that rather than urgency. It is included here because it is well-specified enough to hand to an LLM session as-is, unlike the Analysis page or cross-pane drag-to-transplant (both excluded from this list as genuinely not ready yet).

Context from AGENTS.md: the Planner canvas (packages/ui/src/components/canvas) currently renders with Konva (vanilla, not svelte-konva), with components manually syncing Svelte reactive state into Konva's imperative scene graph. The app's actual usage of Konva does not touch its differentiating features - no Transformer, image filters, caching, or pixel hit-testing; Geometry is limited to four parametric shapes, and resize handles are already a hand-rolled DOM overlay, not Konva's.

Build: replace the Konva scene graph with SVG rendered directly through Svelte reactivity, removing the imperative sync layer entirely. This also directly enables two things specified elsewhere in the design docs that are blocked on it: (1) the planned SVG-based Cultivar IconPack rendering (see design/cultivars/models.md#iconpack-provisional and the GrowthStage/IconPack task) - SVG icon packs can render natively instead of needing a Konva.Image raster-conversion step; (2) the multi-workspace cross-pane drag-to-transplant interaction (see design/planner/wireframes.md#multiple-workspaces) - real DOM nodes let each Workspace be its own positioned g/nested svg, so detecting a drag crossing from one Workspace tile into another is ordinary DOM geometry instead of manually converting pointer coordinates between separate Konva Stage coordinate systems.

If large-farm scenes ever make SVG node count a real bottleneck, the documented fallback is viewport culling and level-of-detail rendering (mirroring the viewport-clipped approach grid.svelte.ts already uses for gridlines) before reaching for a canvas library again - don't reach for that preemptively.

Read AGENTS.md's Architecture Notes section (the Planner canvas bullet) before starting - it is the canonical spec for this migration's scope and reasoning.

Out of scope: the cross-pane drag interaction itself and the IconPack rendering itself (both separate tasks that this one unblocks, not part of it).

Title: Add a Stamp mode toggle to Add Plants
Description:
Context: PlantsCreateFormModeSingle.svelte/CreatePlantContainer.svelte only support what this session's work called 'drag mode' - one live preview that the user repositions by dragging and commits via the Create button, with the seeding effect regenerating or translating it as cultivar/anchor/focused-day change. There is no 'stamp mode' where clicking the canvas immediately stages a plant at that point and starts a fresh preview for the next click - this was scoped out of this session's work on purpose.

Build: a placementMode ('drag' | 'stamp') piece of state on verdagraphContext, following the existing factory-function-with-getters convention selectionManager.svelte.ts/timelineSelection.svelte.ts use (not the dead tool: 'pointer' | 'group' scaffolding on selectionManager, which nothing reads today). Add a toggle near the Mode select in PlantsCreateForm.svelte. In Stamp mode, Canvas.svelte needs a native click handler (not pointerdown/pointerup, to naturally exclude drags - mirror how EditableShape.svelte already distinguishes a click from a drag via its own dragOccurred flag), active only while Add Plants is the tool and Stamp mode is selected: on click, convert the point via localPixelPositionFromPointerEvent + modelXPos/modelYPos (existing canvas transform utilities), set it as the current stamp's location coordinate, and immediately submit via the existing plantsCreateHandler.execute path (the same path the Create button already uses) - the existing stamp carry-forward effect in verdagraphContext.svelte.ts's onUpdated then seeds the next click's starting point automatically. Needs panning disabled while Stamp mode is active - Canvas.svelte's handlePointerDown currently starts a pan on every background pointerdown; gate it on !stampModeActive.

Depends on: none - builds directly on this session's expected-geometry generation and stamp carry-forward work, already in place.

Title: Ghost styling for staged (draft) plants
Description:
Context: a draft (uncommitted, staged in an open DraftBucket) plant renders identically to a committed one everywhere - Layout, Calendar, Tree. isDraftPlant (packages/models/src/plants/queries.ts) already exists and is used this session to gate Recorded Lifespan out of the tree for draft plants, but nothing uses it for visual styling yet, so there's no way to tell staged and committed plants apart at a glance in the Layout.

Build: thread a draft: boolean prop down EditablePlantContainer.svelte -> Plant.svelte -> EditableShape.svelte, extending the pattern selected already uses (Plant.svelte's existing derived style ternaries) - add opacity as a new derived value, reduced when draft is true. EditableShape.svelte already hardcodes opacity={0.7} on one shape variant unrelated to draft state - generalize that into the new draft-driven prop instead of leaving the hardcoded value in place. Add a small corner-badge overlay shown only when draft is true - getShapeAttributes (canvas/utils/shapes.ts) returns a different shape per geometry type with no unified bounding-box helper today (rect gets {x,y,width,height}, ellipse only {rx,ry}, polygon/lines only point strings), so add a small per-type 'top-right corner in local pixels' case (in shapes.ts, or inline in EditableShape.svelte which already branches on shapeAttributes.type), then render a small fixed-size badge <g> at that point. Also worth considering while touching this: merging CreatePlantContainer.svelte/CreatePlantsContainer.svelte (the live unsubmitted-stamp preview, reading $formData directly) with this same ghost-styled rendering of already-staged rows from any visible DraftBucket into one DraftPlantContainer component, since both represent the same 'not yet committed' concept via two separate rendering paths today.

Depends on: isDraftPlant (already built, this session).

Title: Add a per-DraftBucket visibility toggle to the Toolbar
Description:
Context: verdagraphContext.draftBuckets.isVisible(bucketId)/toggleVisible(bucketId) (packages/ui/src/components/verdagraph/verdagraphContext.svelte.ts) already track which open DraftBuckets besides the active one should render as ghosts in Layout/Calendar - auto-seeded so a user's own buckets show by default, other users' need an explicit opt-in. No UI reads or writes this state yet.

Build: a checklist somewhere in the Toolbar (or wherever Layout/Calendar-wide view settings live, see paneSettings.svelte.ts for the existing pattern) listing every open DraftBucket (verdagraphContext.draftBuckets.list) with a checkbox bound to isVisible(bucket.id) / toggleVisible(bucket.id), labeling a bucket with its creator's username when it isn't the current user's own (bucket.creatorId !== ctx.client.profile?.id).

Depends on: the ghost styling task, to have something worth toggling the visibility of.

Title: Calendar drag-to-reschedule for staged plants
Description:
Context: the Calendar (packages/ui/src/components/rangeCalendar/) has no drag interaction of any kind today. The existing move-by-day/week buttons live in an info-point popup and only shift one observation's date - unrelated machinery. Rescheduling a Plant's whole geometry/location history has no code path at all; plants.beginDate/endDate are only ever set once, at creation, in plantsCreateSingle (packages/models/src/plants/controller.ts).

Build: a new controller function plantReschedule(id, deltaDays, ctx) in packages/models/src/plants/controller.ts - in one transaction, shift every geometry's and location's date in the Plant's (expected, for a staged plant) lifespan by deltaDays using the addDays helper (packages/models/src/plants/generation.ts, already exported from this session's work), then recompute plants.beginDate/endDate via the existing historyGetRange utility over the shifted set. Write it generally (shifts the whole set, not just one entry), even though staged plants today only ever have the one generated geometry chain. New drag handling on the Plant's bar in RangeCalendarPane.svelte (hand-rolled pointer events, mirroring EditableShape.svelte's capture -> live override -> commit-on-release pattern already established in the canvas code): onpointerdown captures the pointer and start X; onpointermove computes a pixel delta against the already-available sectionWidthPx, rounds to a day-delta, optimistically overrides the rendered bar position; onpointerup calls plantReschedule with the final day-delta and clears the override.

Scope: wire this for staged (draft) plants first - nothing about the command is draft-specific, so extending it to committed plants later is just exposing the same drag affordance more broadly, not new backend work.

Title: Auto-managed multi-workspace transplant locations
Description:
Context: the expected-geometry/location generation system (packages/models/src/plants/generation.ts) built this session generates a full milestone-based geometry history, but only ever ONE location entry, dated at the anchor - a deliberate V1 scope decision made this session. The real future need, raised during this session's design discussion, is being able to set one workspace to seed a plant in and a different workspace to transplant it into, with the location history auto-generating two entries (one per workspace, at the right dates) instead of one manually-placed location that has to represent the plant's entire life.

Build: extend generateExpectedHistories's params to optionally accept a second (transplant-destination) workspaceId + coordinate for SEED_TO_TRANSPLANT-origin plants, generating two location entries - the seed workspace/coordinate dated at the Seed milestone, the transplant workspace/coordinate dated at the Transplant milestone - instead of the current single entry dated at the anchor. Needs a second placement affordance in PlantsCreateFormModeSingle.svelte/CreatePlantContainer.svelte for the transplant-destination position, alongside the existing single drag target.

Depends on: the Origin picker task - this only matters once SEED_TO_TRANSPLANT is actually reachable from the UI.

Title: Perennial dormancy-cycle generation
Description:
Context: ExpectedGeometryProfile (packages/models/src/cultivars/attributes/geometry/schema.ts) already has exitDormancySize/enterDormancySize fields, and AnnualLifecycleMilestone (packages/models/src/plants/generation.ts) was deliberately named and scoped this session to leave room for this, but generateExpectedHistories only ever produces the single linear annual Seed-to-Expiry chain - dormancy entries are never auto-generated. This was an explicit scope decision confirmed with the user this session: recurring dormancy across a perennial's multi-year life needs real calendar-date logic tied to frost dates, not simple day-offsets from one sowing anchor, which is a materially different and larger feature than the linear annual chain this session built.

Build: a separate milestone/date model for perennial dormancy cycling - likely keyed off FrostDatePlantingWindowsProfile (packages/models/src/cultivars/attributes/frostDatePlantingWindows) rather than day-offsets from a single anchor, since dormancy is calendar-seasonal and recurs yearly rather than happening once per plant.
